question: What is the primary function of an epidemiological reservoir for a pathogen?

options.A: To block the transmission cycle permanently
options.B: To provide a place to live and multiply
options.C: To artificially manufacture new synthetic antibodies
options.D: To destroy the infectious agent completely

explanation: Pathogens depend on reservoirs as natural habitats where they can survive, reproduce, and maintain their species over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h1)

question: Why can a healthy-looking person still act as an epidemiological reservoir?

options.A: They only carry dead microorganisms that cannot cause harm
options.B: Their body temperature is too high for the pathogen to grow
options.C: They harbor and multiply the pathogen without showing illness
options.D: Their immune system destroys the agent before symptoms start

explanation: Asymptomatic carriers harbor infectious agents and shed them into the environment while appearing completely healthy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h1)

question: Which category of reservoir includes soil, water, and vegetation?
explanation: Non-living elements like soil and water act as environmental reservoirs where certain pathogens naturally reside. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h2)

question: A patient contracts rabies after being bitten by a stray dog. What type of reservoir is the dog?
explanation: Animals serve as zoonotic reservoirs when they harbor pathogens that can cross the species barrier to infect humans. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h2)

question: Treating an infected patient with antibiotics primarily disrupts which part of the chain of infection?
explanation: Treating the infected person eliminates or reduces the pathogen inside the human reservoir, stopping the chain at its source. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h3)

question: What is the primary animal reservoir for the Lassa virus in Nigeria?
explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys natalensis) serves as the primary natural reservoir and shedding source for the Lassa fever virus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h4)

question: Why do zoonotic diseases pose a significant public health risk in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Complete lack of modern diagnostic equipment in cities
options.B: High rates of mosquito breeding in dry desert sands
options.C: Close daily contact between humans and animal reservoirs
options.D: Strict laws banning the consumption of local livestock

explanation: Farming, livestock rearing, and shared living spaces increase human exposure to animal reservoirs and zoonotic pathogens. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h4)

question: Who is typically the first healthcare worker to notice unusual disease clusters in rural communities?
explanation: Nurses working in primary health care interact directly with patients daily, making them the first to spot unusual disease patterns. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of tracing an index case during a disease investigation?

options.A: To punish the patient for breaking public health laws
options.B: To replace standard hospital admission registers
options.C: To manufacture synthetic vaccines for local clinics
options.D: To identify the original infection source or reservoir

explanation: Tracing index cases helps public health teams locate the primary reservoir and prevent ongoing transmission in the community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h5)

question: Which intervention is commonly used to manage an animal reservoir like dogs during a rabies outbreak?
explanation: Vaccinating animal populations, such as dogs, builds herd immunity and directly controls the zoonotic reservoir. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h6)

question: Why is targeting the reservoir often more effective than protecting every susceptible host?

options.A: It is much cheaper than buying any hospital medications
options.B: It eliminates the source, stopping new infections at the root
options.C: It prevents the need for any handwashing in the wards
options.D: It guarantees that humans will never catch a virus again

explanation: Removing or treating the reservoir stops the pathogen production line entirely, protecting the whole population at once. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h6)

question: Which nursing action helps control environmental reservoirs within a hospital setting?

options.A: Keeping windows locked permanently during the day
options.B: Proper biomedical waste disposal and hand hygiene
options.C: Refusing to admit patients with chronic illnesses
options.D: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every visitor

explanation: Infection control practices like waste management and hand hygiene prevent pathogens from spreading via environmental reservoirs in hospitals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h7)

question: How do nurses extend reservoir-focused disease prevention beyond the hospital walls?

options.A: By performing major surgeries inside local community markets
options.B: By closing down local water boreholes during rainy seasons
options.C: By educating families on home sanitation and rodent control
options.D: By banning all livestock farming across the entire country

explanation: Nurses educate communities on practical steps like covering food and water safety to minimize domestic exposure to reservoirs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h7)
